80584.subject: Turbulence in France
80584.body:
Editor's Digest 

Автор: Financial Times


Автор: Financial Times

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/turbulence-france-financial-times-wngqc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BOz8TL4PsR%2FCW95x1g%2FyCug%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2OueQLzK7hEss1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mv233j59~e3-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mv233j59-e3
  
Emmanuel Macron is used to political turbulence, whether it’s turning over prime ministers or confronting street protests. This week the pressure on his minority government escalated to a new extreme. Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators, many of them students, marched on cities across France to protest against the lamentable state of public schools — a compliant that has been simmering for years. The government, however, cannot turn to its usual method of calming protests — taking out the cheque book. France needs belt-tightening: it is suffering from a brutal sell-off in the country’s bonds, which have taken borrowing costs to their highest level in almost a quarter of a century. The turbulence on the streets and in the markets is happening in the run-up to next year’s presidential election, in which the far right’s Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner. This is a story to watch. I’m off to Paris on Monday and I’ll report back on what I find next week. My choices this week After a year of timorous efforts to out-Farage Nigel Farage, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has decided to go her own way. Our UK chief political commentator Robert Shrimsley examines Badenoch’s punchy plan to reunite the right. Across the world, parenthood is on the wane. Camilla Cavendish explains how social contagion can help explain falling birth rates — and offer a way out of the demographic trap. (Free to read) Our new series examines China’s breakneck build-out of AI infrastructure as it seeks to become the pre-eminent tech superpower. In the first of three instalments, we explore Inner Mongolia’s vast new computing hubs. Hedge funds’ insatiable demand for financing has made them irresistible clients for lenders. But as banks lean into the trading boom, they have inextricably bound their fates with their biggest clients. Here’s a question: “If you are a man who cares about climate change, are you a bit of a dweeb?” Our climate columnist Pilita Clark explores the gender differences in how people think about global warming. Hyperliquid Labs is one of the hottest names in crypto. But its products, described by some as “the most dangerous” in the industry, are raising the heat in Singapore, a city-state averse to risk where Hyperliquid has made its home. (Free to read) Thanks for reading, Roula Khalaf, FT editor Recommended newsletters for you White House Watch What Trump’s second ter

80536.subject: How Avalanche Is Entering the Next Era of Tokenized Finance
80536.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/how-avalanche-is-entering-the-next

For years, much of the conversation around tokenized finance has centered on the same assets: U.S. Treasuries, money market funds, and stablecoins.
They made sense as an entry point. These are familiar financial products with established demand, relatively straightforward structures, and deep liquidity. Putting them onchain demonstrated that traditional financial assets could exist within blockchain-based infrastructure.
But the market is starting to move further up the financial stack.
The latest example comes from Securitize and Neuberger Berman.
On August 18, Securitize announced the launch of the Neuberger Securitize High Income Tokenized Fund (HINC), a new tokenized fixed-income fund available across Avalanche and other three major networks.
The fund primarily invests in high-yield bonds while also gaining exposure to other income-producing assets, including collateralized loan obligations and leveraged loans. Behind the strategy is Neuberger Berman, whose fixed-income platform oversees more than $230 billion in assets.
The more interesting part, however, is what the fund represents for the broader evolution of tokenized finance.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Tokenization Is Moving Into Credit
The first phase of tokenization was largely about proving that familiar financial assets could be represented onchain.
HINC points toward a more ambitious use case: bringing actively managed and more complex financial strategies into blockchain-based infrastructure.
Neuberger Berman is contributing its fixed-income portfolio management and research expertise as subadvisor, while Securitize provides the infrastructure around the tokenized fund, including issuance, administration, and distribution.
The underlying investment strategy is still a traditional fixed-income strategy. What changes is the infrastructure through which investors can access and interact with the product.
That distinction matters because credit introduces considerably more complexity than simply representing a Treasury or money market fund onchain.
High-yield bonds, leveraged loans, and CLOs require credit analysis, portfolio construction, risk management, liquidity considerations, and active management. Bringing these products into a tokenized environment therefore tests whether blockchain infrastructure can support financial products with significantly more moving parts.
That is where the next phase of tokenization becomes interesting. If increasingly sophisticated financial products can operate through blockchain infrastructure, tokenization begins to look less like a niche digital-asset experiment and more like another component of financial market infrastructure.
Why Avalanche Matters
HINC is launching across four public blockchain networks, including Avalanche.
